title: Investment, advice AFCA complaints up 56% in FY26
full_text:
The Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) has released its outcomes for the 2025/26 financial year, with investments and advice-related complaints reported the biggest jump.
AFCA has reported its third consecutive year with more than 100,000 complaints after Australians lodged 119,949 in FY26 for the highest year on record.
While banking and finance made up more than half (55.8 per cent) of the complaints for this period – racking up 66,971 – investments and advice saw the biggest jump in FY26, increasing 56 per cent to 6,542.
This increase was largely attributed to the Shield Master Fund and First Guardian collapses as complaints alleging failure to act in the client’s best interest jumped 65 per cent to 2,081 to account for almost a third (31.8 per cent) of all investments and advice-related complaints, making it the top driver for the sector in FY26.
AFCA chief customer officer Deborah Jenkins said: “While most financial advice firms do the right thing, we are seeing a significant number of complaints stem from major financial collapses that have affected thousands of consumers. These matters are complex and can be incredibly stressful for individuals and their families.”
This is evident on the AFCA Datacube which shows that 1,395 complaints were filed against InterPrac Financial Planning in FY26, making it the biggest recipient of complaints within the advice industry.
The runner up was significantly behind with Financial Services Group Australia receiving 469, followed by Uniter Global Capital at 365, MWL Financial Services with 252 and Next Generation Advice at 73. Of the top five firms, InterPrac is the only one not in liquidation.
Meanwhile, superannuation complaints also saw a significant jump with 8,755 reported for an increase of 42 per cent compared with the previous financial year. Delays in claim handling, service issues and rejection of super insurance claims were the most common issues raised, the latter of which saw an 82 per cent increase from FY25.

Source: AFCA, August 2026
Jenkins said: “These numbers highlight the impact that ongoing cost-of-living challenges and economic uncertainty are having on consumers, and the flow-on effects these conditions can have across the financial system,” Jenkins said.
“Every complaint represents someone’s experience, and collectively they provide a view of where consumers are struggling. By working with us and acting on these insights, firms can help prevent recurring issues that lead to complaints with AFCA.
“These numbers point to opportunities for firms to strengthen hardship support, improve communication with customers and ensure accurate credit reporting, helping resolve issues before they become disputes.”
author: Shy-Ann Arkinstall
